4. **Cause (b) of the #2254 miss - GRAMMAR GAP in check 28.** The four

   >=3 hyphen segments with a digit-bearing tail. So even WITH a `text`
   block, check 28 would not have flagged `per_question_dots.png`.

- **Must-Fix 1 (accepted).** v2 keyed check 60's textlessness predicate on
  `_iter_meta_label_values(meta)` over the whole sidecar. `inputs` is not in
  `_META_PROVENANCE_KEYS`, so #2254's realized sidecars yield their input-path
  strings and would have read as text-bearing — check 60 would have been
  SILENT on the exact incident set it was written for. v3 keys the predicate on
  the `text` block itself, which also makes the check and the 60.9%-textless
  posture measurement the same instrument.
- **Must-Fix 2 (accepted).** `_opaque_code_tokens` has TWO consumers: check 28
  (WARN) and check 57 Leg A (FAIL, v4, not date-gated). v2's plan to add the
  new class to the shared tuple would have created a new hard promote-time FAIL
  path, violating its own AC5 and silently touching a check the plan fences
  off. v3 makes class (h) check-28-local; `_opaque_code_tokens` stays
  byte-stable (new AC3 + a call-site-set regression pin).
- **Should-Fix 3 (accepted).** v2's claim that `_is_path_like_word` already
  excludes email-shaped `user@example.com` was mechanically wrong (that
  predicate returns False for any slash-free word). v3 adds a `(?!\.[a-z])`
  lookahead, which is what actually excludes them.
- **Should-Fix 4 (accepted) — and it fired K1.** The critic replaced v2's
  >=20-promoted-body FP probe with the full 3,560-sidecar corpus sweep and RAN
